name: Tiendanube
tagline: Hosted ecommerce platform for Latin American merchants, storefront plus checkout plus payments and shipping integrations.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The storefront is the easy half: product grid, cart, theme, done in an afternoon. The hard half is everything behind the buy button, which in Latin America means Mercado Pago, Pix, boleto, local card acquirers, installments (cuotas, parcelamento), correios and local carrier labels, plus tax documents that vary by country. You can wire one payment provider yourself, but you are now the one handling PCI scope, chargebacks, refunds, fraud rules and the fact that customers only trust checkouts that look like checkouts they have seen before. Themes being community-driven is true and also irrelevant: nobody pays Tiendanube for the theme. You would be building a small payments and logistics integration business to avoid a subscription that costs less than a day of your time.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted product catalog with a cart that ends in a hosted payment link you paste in per product, plus a local order list.
requirements: A payment provider account if you want real money to move, e.g. Mercado Pago or Stripe
Somewhere to host it with HTTPS, because no one types a card number on http
Your own product photos and copy
whatYouLose: Local payment methods that LatAm buyers actually use: Pix, boleto, cash networks, card installments
Carrier integrations and prepaid shipping labels, so fulfillment goes back to manual
PCI scope, fraud screening and chargeback handling becoming somebody else's problem
Checkout conversion polish: abandoned cart recovery, address autofill, trust signals buyers recognize
App ecosystem and the marketplace of local apps, themes and agencies that plug straight in
moatNotes: The regional specificity is the product. A generic store builder with Stripe is not a substitute in markets where half of checkouts are Pix or boleto.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the subscription is a rounding error next to the cost of getting payments wrong once. A merchant doing real volume needs installments, local payment rails, tax paperwork that an accountant will accept, and a checkout that converts strangers. Tiendanube has spent years negotiating those integrations per country and keeping them working when a provider changes an API. You can replicate the shopfront in a weekend and then spend six months on the parts nobody sees.
notes: The storefront is a weekend; the checkout is a company. The moat is local payment rails, carrier integrations and per-country tax compliance, none of which an agent can one-shot.
prompt:
Build a small self-hosted online store for a single merchant. Stack: Next.js (App Router, TypeScript), SQLite via better-sqlite3, Tailwind for styling. No external services beyond one payment provider.

In scope:
- A products table: id, slug, title, description (markdown), price_cents, currency, image paths, stock, active flag, optional external_payment_url.
- A seed script that loads products from a local products.json file, and images from ./public/products.
- Public pages: home with a product grid, /p/[slug] product detail, /cart, /checkout.
- Cart stored in a signed httpOnly cookie, no login, no user accounts.
- Checkout flow: collect name, email, shipping address, write an order row with line items and status 'pending', then redirect the buyer to the payment URL. If a product has external_payment_url, use it directly. Otherwise, if STRIPE_SECRET_KEY is set in .env, create a Stripe Checkout Session server side for the cart and redirect there.
- A Stripe webhook route at /api/webhooks/stripe that verifies the signature with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET and flips the matching order to 'paid'. If no key is configured, skip this route cleanly instead of crashing.
- An admin area at /admin protected by a single ADMIN_PASSWORD from .env using basic auth middleware: list orders, mark as shipped, add a tracking number, edit stock.
- Order confirmation page and a plain text email body printed to the server log, no email provider.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-currency, installments, tax or invoice generation, carrier label printing, discount engines, multi-vendor, themes, analytics, any telemetry.

Rules: all secrets in .env with a committed .env.example, never hardcoded. Store prices as integers in cents. Validate all form input server side with zod. Ship a README with setup, seed, and a note that this handles no PCI data itself because cards are entered on the provider's page. Include seed data for three fake products so `npm run dev` shows a working store immediately.
